cases.evidence_note: p590b p. 29, Additional 10% Tax, Example: "Tom Jones, who is 35 years old, receives a $3,000 distribution from his traditional IRA account. Tom doesn't meet any of the exceptions to the 10% additional tax, so the $3,000 is an early distribution. Tom never made any nondeductible contributions to his IRA. ... Tom must also pay an additional tax of $300 (10% (0.10) × $3,000)." The filled-in Form 5329 (p590b p. 32) shows line 1 3000, line 2 -0-, line 3 3000, line 4 300. Class A covers Form 5329 lines 1 to 4 and the $3,000 on Form 1040 line 4b; Schedule 2 line 8 $300 follows from line 4 (f5329 line 4, "Include this amount on Schedule 2 (Form 1040), line 8"). Not asserted: whether Form 5329 is filed and the line 8 box. The example says "He files Form 5329"; the project (D5) takes the no-form path for a code 1 distribution with no exception (i5329 p. 1), so the tax is the same but the form is not prepared. Synthetic scaffolding (not in the example): single, wages $50,000 (the stage18.blind.p1 base with its Marketplace coverage removed, and the Form 1099-R entry of stage10.ira.fully_taxable); Form 1099-R box 7 code 1, the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box checked, nothing rolled over, no case on the entry screen.

p970 p. 56, chapter 8, Example 1: a teacher (age 32) paid $5,800 of qualified education expenses from $5,000 of tax-free employer-provided educational assistance and an "Early distribution from IRA (taxable part is $500) . . . 3,200"; "Equals: AQEE $ 800"; "Because the teacher’s AQEE ($800) is more than the taxable part of their IRA distribution ($500), they don't have to pay the 10% additional tax on any part of this distribution. However, they must include the $500 taxable earnings in their gross income subject to income tax." Class A covers $500 in income, no additional tax (Form 5329 line 4 $0). Lines 1 $500, 2 $500 (exception 08) and 3 $0 follow from i5329 p. 5 (line 2, "the amount that you can exclude"); Schedule 2 line 8 $0 and Form 5329 filed (an exception is claimed, i5329 p. 1) follow from the form. Synthetic scaffolding (not in the example): single, wages $50,000 (the stage18.blind.p1 base with its Marketplace coverage removed, and the Form 1099-R entry of stage10.ira.fully_taxable); code 1. The example's $2,700 nontaxable part is a return of nondeductible contributions (basis, Form 8606), which retirement.special refuses; the scaffold therefore enters a $500 distribution with no basis, so Form 1040 line 4a (gross $3,200 in the example) is not asserted. The $5,000 tax-free assistance enters only through the AQEE, entered as the exception 08 amount $800.

Mutation regression (refusal.s2.s2.line8.0), predicted by hand before recording. Blind return E7 (joint; exception 05 claimed for $5,000 by the taxpayer and $3,000 by the spouse) with medical expenses of $15,775. AGI $117,000, 7.5% = $8,775, so Schedule A line 4 is $7,000. i5329 p. 5, Line 2: "up to the amount you paid for unreimbursed medical expenses during the year minus 7.5% of your adjusted gross income (AGI)". T-068. Inputs are the answers the full interview asked of a single filer with one W-2 ($20,000 wages) and no Schedule C, which it now asks for s179.line10 because s179.line13 (the carryover to 2026) is a target of the full profile. Predicted by hand before recording: a $3,000 carryover from line 13 of the 2024 Form 4562; line 11 is the smaller of line 5 ($2,500,000) and business income including wages ($20,000), so the income limit alone would not stop a deduction, but no Schedule C is on the return to take it (i4562 p. 5, Line 12, "enter the amount allocated to the business or activity"), so line 13 refuses at s179.orphan.

s179.line13.form: A section 179 carryover from 2024 with no business on the return
s179.line13.remedy: Deducting a section 179 carryover without a Schedule C business is outside this tool.

cite.locator: p. 5, Lines 10 to 12

cases.evidence_note: T-068 companion. The same filer answering zero to the carryover question: the gate is false and line 13, reported to the full profile, is $0.00 (lines 9 and 10 are zero). Predicted by hand before recording.

T-073. Inputs are stage16.refuse.f2441.employer_care with both children's care expenses set to $0: the employer furnished the care, box 10 is $2,000 and the filer paid nothing. Before the fix f2441.employer_care_gate (which needs paid expenses) was false, line 16 was $0.00, line 17 $0.00 and line 26 the whole $2,000. Whether the value of employer-furnished care is a qualified expense incurred for line 16 is not stated in i2441 (p. 5, Line 16; p. 3, Columns (a) and (b)) or Pub. 503 (p. 10, Dependent Care Benefits), so line 17 now refuses at f2441.employer_care_l16 (line 16 $0 less than line 15 $2,000), and line 26 with it. Predicted by hand before recording.

f2441.line17.remedy: Your employer furnished care whose value is among your dependent care benefits, and the expenses you entered are less than your benefits. The instructions do not say whether the value of the care your employer furnished is a qualified expense incurred for line 16, and that decides how much of your benefits is excluded; this tool does not figure that case.

cite.locator: p. 5, Line 16, "Enter the total of all qualified expenses incurred in 2025 for the care of your qualifying person(s)"; p. 1, Dependent Care Benefits, "The fair market value of care in a daycare facility provided or sponsored by your employer"; p. 3, Columns (a) and (b), "If you were covered by your employer's dependent care plan and your employer furnished the care (either at your workplace or by hiring a care provider), enter your employer's name in column (a)"

f2441.line26.remedy: Your employer furnished care whose value is among your dependent care benefits, and the expenses you entered are less than your benefits. The instructions do not say whether the value of the care your employer furnished is a qualified expense incurred for line 16, and that decides how much of your benefits is excluded; this tool does not figure that case.

cite.locator: p. 5, Line 16, "Enter the total of all qualified expenses incurred in 2025 for the care of your qualifying person(s)"; p. 1, Dependent Care Benefits, "The fair market value of care in a daycare facility provided or sponsored by your employer"; p. 3, Columns (a) and (b), "If you were covered by your employer's dependent care plan and your employer furnished the care (either at your workplace or by hiring a care provider), enter your employer's name in column (a)"

cases.evidence_note: T-073 boundary. stage16.refuse.f2441.employer_care with $1,000 paid for each child: line 16 ($2,000) equals line 15 ($2,000), so the reading of line 16 cannot change line 17 and the new gate is false; line 17 is $2,000.00 and line 26 $0.00. Line 30 still refuses at f2441.employer_care_gate (expenses paid with employer-furnished care). Predicted by hand before recording.

f2441.line30.remedy: When your employer furnished care and you also paid for care, the value of the employer's care is among your benefits but is not an expense you paid, and the instructions do not say how line 30 treats it; this tool does not figure that case.

cite.locator: p. 3, Columns (a) and (b), "enter your employer's name in column (a)"
